I read the whole file and checked the related uses of `posSemidef` and `isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub` in the PositiveDefinite directory.

The only substantial repetition is in `IsPositiveDefiniteSub.posSemidef` and `of_posSemidef`. Both reindex a kernel along the identity equivalence `G ≃ WithNegStar G` using `Matrix.submatrix`, and both prove a `heq` by `ext; simp [sub_eq_add_neg]`. This is mirror-image code of about 8 lines each. A shared iff lemma would still have to prove both directions, so it would only move the two branches into a helper. That is not enough under the rubric.

Many other declarations share the shape `isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite.mpr (generic lemma ...)`. These are thin wrappers around existing generic API. The `simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using hF.isPositiveDefinite.…` proofs are short routine transfers. `comp_addMonoidHom`, `comp_smul` and `comp_neg` are short calculations. None of these meets the bar of nontrivial repeated reasoning.

I found no justified finding. One remaining uncertainty is that a similar reindexing pattern appears in `SemigroupGroup/Time/Slice/Basic.lean`. That file is outside the target and the shared piece is small, so I did not report it.
